attributes.h5_api_gap: src/h5/api.ts's AttrValue union omits `bigint`; it needs adding, or attrsAt()/attrs() must narrow BigInt to Number at the boundary.
attributes.note: An int64 attribute arrives as a JS BigInt, an int32 attribute as a Number, and a variable-bin file's bin-size as the string 'null'. All three reach the `_int_attr` mirror, so it must accept bigint — `typeof v === 'number'` is false for 1000n, and `Number('null')` is NaN while `Boolean('null')` is true. See the `attrs` block of basic.metacool (int64), floatcount.metacool (int32) and variable.metacool (string 'null').

dtype_strings.note: h5wasm's Dataset.dtype is C-struct-style, not numpy-style: int64 is '<q', int32 '<i', float64 '<d', fixed-length strings 'A<n>', vlen strings 'S'. The `dtype` fields in these goldens are numpy strings ('<i8', '<i4', '<f8', '|S12') and the `kind` fields are numpy kinds. Map through `kind_by_h5wasm_letter` before comparing; do not slice dtype[1] and expect a numpy kind.

non_finite.note: Optional /genomes columns carry NaN for any genome absent from the user's --genomes table (__unbinned__ always is, since /genomes rows are derived from the contigs table and the table only left-joins). JSON has no NaN, so these goldens encode it as null; the JS reader will see a real NaN and must treat the two as equal. metadata.metacool is the fixture with this shape.

string_decoding.note: h5wasm decodes fixed-length 'A<n>' string datasets as Latin-1, not UTF-8: /contigs/name in utf8.metacool comes back as 'contig_Ã±_04' where the file holds 'contig_ñ_04'. Dataset.value is therefore unusable for name columns — read the raw bytes and decode with TextDecoder('utf-8'), stripping trailing NULs (spec §6.2). utf8.metacool and utf8_genomes.metacool exist to fail loudly on this.
